title: Largest Value Paired With Its Opposite
statement:
You get an integer array nums that contains no zeros. Find the largest positive value k such that both k and -k appear in nums.

Return k, or -1 if no positive value has its negative in the array.

examples.why: 9 is the largest value, but -9 is missing. 7 and 3 both have partners, and 7 is larger.
-4 has no 4, and 5 and 8 have no negatives.
The largest absolute value, 6, only appears as a negative. Duplicates change nothing.

hints: For each positive value, you only need to know whether its negative is somewhere in the array.
Answering "is -k present?" quickly is a set lookup.
Put every value in a set. Scan the positives, keep the largest one whose negative is in the set. Alternatively, sort and close in from both ends.

explain.intuition:
The question for each positive k is a membership test: is -k in the array? A hash set answers that in O(1), so one pass to build the set and one pass to check every positive is enough.

A sorting version is also neat. After sorting, the most negative values sit on the left and the largest positives on the right. Compare -nums[lo] with nums[hi]: if they match you have found the largest pair; if the negative side is bigger in size, it can never match anything larger, so move lo; otherwise move hi.
steps: Add every value to a set.
For each positive value v, if the set contains -v, set best = max(best, v).
pitfalls: Returning the largest value overall, or the largest absolute value, without checking that its partner exists.
Returning 0 or a negative number when nothing pairs. The answer for no pair is exactly -1.
Matching a value with itself. With no zeros this cannot happen for a correct check, but a careless abs comparison can count -5, -5 as a pair.

solutions.title: Check every pair
solutions.idea: For every positive value, search the whole array for its negative.

solutions.title: Sort and close in
solutions.idea: Sorted, the strongest negatives are on the left and the largest positives on the right. Drop whichever side is larger in size until they match.

solutions.title: Hash set
solutions.idea: Store all values, then keep the largest positive whose negative is stored.

followups: Count how many distinct values k have both k and -k present.
The array is a stream too large to store. What can you keep if values are bounded by 100 000?
lcTitle: Largest Positive Integer That Exists With Its Negative
